chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Hakam, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying:

Al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah, when testimony was given against him for drinking wine, ʿUthmān said to ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘Judge between him and these who claim that he drank wine.’ So ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered, and he was flogged with a whip having two branches, forty lashes.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ جَلْدَةً: forty lashes; the number of lashes administered
key_terms.اقْضِ: judge; issue a legal ruling between disputing parties
key_terms.سَوْطٍ: whip; the instrument used for flogging
key_terms.شُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ: drinking wine; the offense under discussion
key_terms.شُعْبَتَانِ: two branches; describing the whip used
key_terms.فَجُلِدَ: he was flogged; the prescribed corporal punishment was carried out

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Imam ʿAlī’s judgment regarding the punishment for drinking wine?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts an incident in which al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah was accused of drinking wine, and ʿUthmān referred the matter to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام for judgment. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered that the punishment be carried out as forty lashes, reflecting the legal handling of intoxication in early Islamic governance.
